runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current GOV.UK NPPF/Planning Inspectorate readback, explicit effective-date handling and separation of authority-wide supply tests from parcel deliverability.

sources.label: NPPF Section 2
sources.fact: Paragraphs 10-12 retain the presumption in favour of sustainable development while the statutory development plan remains the starting point for decisions.

sources.label: NPPF Section 5 land supply
sources.fact: Plans should identify specific deliverable sites for years 1-5 and developable sites/broad locations for later years.

sources.label: NPPF five-year supply
sources.fact: Authorities should update annually a minimum five-year supply of deliverable sites against the applicable requirement/local housing need.

sources.label: NPPF 1 July 2026 buffer
sources.fact: From 1 July 2026 a 20% decision-making buffer applies in the specified adopted-requirement/80%-of-current-LHN circumstances.

sources.label: NPPF Housing Delivery Test consequences
sources.fact: HDT consequences escalate at below 95%, 85% and 75%; the below-75% threshold engages the presumption in addition to action-plan/buffer consequences.

sources.label: Housing Delivery Test 2023 measurement
sources.fact: Published 12 December 2024; GOV.UK notes a delayed publication timetable and that previously published results remain relevant until superseded.

sources.label: Planning Inspectorate housing land supply evidence
sources.fact: Published 1 June 2026; provides legacy-system templates and stresses version-specific transitional NPPF evidence.

sources.label: Planning Inspectorate deliverable-site evidence
sources.fact: Outline/allocated/brownfield-register major sites require clear evidence that completions will begin within five years to be treated as deliverable under that framework version.

sources.label: Current London Plan status
sources.fact: London Plan 2021 remains the current adopted spatial development strategy while the next plan is prepared.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Chapter 4
sources.fact: Adopted housing policies provide strategic context but do not themselves prove a candidate parcel is deliverable within five years.

sources.label: LBBD Local Plan 2037
sources.fact: Adopted 18 September 2024; parcel delivery still requires current permission, implementation and site-specific evidence.

sources.label: Draft London Plan 2026 homes chapter
sources.fact: Published as Draft in July 2026 and therefore not silently substituted for the adopted 2021 plan in current parcel scoring.

examples.result: Authority-wide five-year supply is not converted into parcel-level delivery probability.
The 1 July 2026 NPPF buffer is applied only where its specific authority-level criteria are evidenced.
Below-75% HDT consequence is not inferred without the applicable published/recalculated authority result.
Brownfield-register or allocation status alone is not treated as five-year deliverability for major sites.
Outline permission requires clear delivery evidence before a major site is counted as deliverable.
The presumption does not erase the statutory starting point of the development plan.
Draft London Plan 2026 housing provisions remain DRAFT and are not substituted for adopted policy.
No candidate promotion occurs without exact parcel relation plus current deliverability/permission evidence.
